original_question: For the two-server queue regimes just described, namely the case rho = 1 with a subexponential service-time distribution and the case rho in (1, 2) with a heavy-tailed service-time distribution having all power moments finite, what are the typical sample paths that lead to large values of the stationary waiting time D?
target_in_paper: Section 1.3, "Rare events": the final unnumbered open problem for the two-server FCFS queue (m = 2), after the discussion of Whitt's conjecture (2), namely the cases (i) rho = 1 with subexponential service times and (ii) 1 < rho < 2 with heavy-tailed service times having all power moments finite, together with the request to identify the typical paths leading to large values of D. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7045455/some-open-problems-related-to-stability-1-multi))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly isolates the two open two-server regimes, keeps the focus on the stationary waiting time D, and asks for the sample-path/rare-event mechanism rather than drifting to a broader stability or general multiserver problem. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7045455/some-open-problems-related-to-stability-1-multi))
missing_details: The queue is a stable two-server FCFS GI/GI/2 system (the paper writes G/G/m and then specializes to m = 2), not an arbitrary two-server model. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7045455/some-open-problems-related-to-stability-1-multi))

Interarrival times {t_n} and service times {sigma_n} are assumed to be two independent i.i.d. sequences. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7045455/some-open-problems-related-to-stability-1-multi))

The load is rho := E[sigma_1]/E[t_1], with the overall stability condition rho < 2; the two open cases are the boundary case rho = 1 and the noninteger case 1 < rho < 2. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7045455/some-open-problems-related-to-stability-1-multi))
D denotes the stationary waiting time in this queue. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7045455/some-open-problems-related-to-stability-1-multi))

The phrase 'large values of D' is asymptotic: the paper is asking about the rare event {D > x} as x -> infinity. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7045455/some-open-problems-related-to-stability-1-multi))

In case (i), the paper only asks for progress 'at least' for some particular subexponential service-time law, with regularly varying distributions given as an example. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7045455/some-open-problems-related-to-stability-1-multi))

In case (ii), 'heavy-tailed' is defined here by the absence of every positive exponential moment, E[e^{c sigma_1}] = infinity for all c > 0, while 'all power moments finite' should be read as E[sigma_1^p] < infinity for every p > 0; the paper gives the stretched-exponential example P(sigma_1 > x) = e^{-x^beta}, beta in (0,1). ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7045455/some-open-problems-related-to-stability-1-multi))

The surrounding rare-event heuristic is that, in Whitt's conjectural picture, large delay comes from a certain number of exceptionally large past service times; your draft does not mention this context. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7045455/some-open-problems-related-to-stability-1-multi))

The exact open-problem block also asks for the asymptotics of P(D > x) in these regimes; your draft keeps only the sample-path half of the paper's formulation. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7045455/some-open-problems-related-to-stability-1-multi))
refined_question: In the stable GI/GI/2 first-come-first-served queue with independent i.i.d. interarrival times {t_n} and service times {sigma_n}, load rho := E[sigma_1]/E[t_1] < 2, and stationary waiting time D, what are the asymptotically typical rare-event sample paths leading to {D > x} as x -> infinity in the two open cases singled out by Foss: (a) rho = 1, at least for some particular subexponential service-time distribution (for example, regularly varying), and (b) 1 < rho < 2 when the service-time distribution is heavy-tailed in the sense that E[e^{c sigma_1}] = infinity for every c > 0 but E[sigma_1^p] < infinity for every p > 0 (for example, P(sigma_1 > x) = e^{-x^beta} with beta in (0,1))? ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7045455/some-open-problems-related-to-stability-1-multi))
justification: This is the narrowest paper-faithful reformulation because Section 1.3 first fixes the i.i.d.-independent and stability assumptions, defines the rare-event target D, recalls Whitt's heuristic that large delays should be driven by a specific number of big past service times, and then specializes to m = 2 and lists exactly the two unresolved regimes appearing in your draft, ending with the request to understand the typical paths producing large D. The nearby unnumbered proposition in Section 1.2 is relevant context because it shows that integer-load cases are already exceptional in the adjacent moment problem. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7045455/some-open-problems-related-to-stability-1-multi))
